quest.title: The Recollector's Path
quest.description: Sorush has finally realized that, at some point, she walked down a path of meaninglessness and absurdity. The training is approaching its conclusion...\n
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x10, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Oh, Sorush, you appear weary. Did you find an obstacle to your progress?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we call it an obstacle or a sense of confusion...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recount what was said during your talk with Sorush to Zurvan...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: I see. However, the records of humans deviating from actual reality isn't anything new. They are a forgetful and prejudiced people, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Considering how vast and complex the affairs of the world generally are, observers might be able to get an overview of the major details but not be able to grasp the minutiae. Those present during said affairs might be direct witnesses, but still find themselves unable to move beyond their personal subjectivity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This doesn't feel very comforting.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Oh. So, you wish for me to provide some warm words to placate Sorush? Did you forget that this is part of her training?

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: To be able to overcome problems by oneself, that's the point of training, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon guesses that makes sense...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: If Sorush cannot meet this task successfully, then all that can be said is she is unworthy of the title of Bloomguard, and will not be able to bear the weight of the Twin-Horned Chaplet.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: And when the time comes, gentle though I am right now, I can only do what must be done. No matter how cruel.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: W—Will you take my Chaplet from me?

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: As for the punishment for failure, I suppose you will discover that yourself, should you truly fail.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm... If Sorush doesn't want to be bald, she better try extra hard now!

talks.objective: Head to the specified location and complete the trial
Head to the specified location and complete the trial

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: It has long been a familiar sight to me, but now I feel only conflicted thinking about it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... On the bright side, this maybe means that Sorush has matured?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I know not if this is growth or a decline instead...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cheer up, Sorush! It's not like you to get so down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! Since we're already here, why don't you tell us about the early history of the Order of Skeptics?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although things are the way they are now... there must've been a point to their establishment, right? Otherwise Zurvan wouldn't have helped them and you wouldn't have been drawn to them.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Very well, if you wish to listen, I will speak... However, you must know that my birth came after the Order of Skeptics was formed. What happened prior is but hearsay to me as well.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: It was said that, before all that transpired, there were some of absolute purity and virtue who attempted to spread the word that catastrophe was imminent.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: But carrying a message does not halt the coming of ruin. Soon, darkness washed over the lands as roiling tides, drowning all that lived in fear.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Just as we saw of the Setekh Wenut, even the strongest creatures were crystallized, perishing during the event.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Comparatively, with how soft and weak humans are, their resulting scouring cannot be considered a personal failing.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: But some individuals arrived, rushing into the maelstrom that was the calamity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Were these people the first Order of Skeptics?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Indeed. Their leader was Nagarjuna. He once was a researcher who worked in the depths of the woods, but he put roots down here to help alleviate the aftershocks of the catastrophe.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Yes, and there was another one with golden hair... Though my elder spoke little of him, he should count as an "interesting" individual, I think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #*sigh*... It's a real shame that he only lived a few hundred years ago. If he was still here, Paimon would love to see him meet {NICKNAME}. Then we can see who's more "interesting."

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Following this, after my birth, the aftereffects of the catastrophe stabilized.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Sorush had nothing to do then?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmph... Not entirely, as the filth will never be fully eradicated. It's just that... noble sacrifices like the one made by the divine bird, Simurgh, were no longer needed.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: What's more, such duties have already been performed by Mihir, Rashnu, and other Pari predating me.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: After Nagarjuna, the Elder slowly broke off contact with the Order of Skeptics. However, the Skeptics themselves remained ever-interested in us Pari.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But I suppose this is nothing strange. To them, after all, we Pari are heroes worthy of songs and odes. The strong feelings of admiration we inspire are more than deserved.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: During that time, I often heard them loudly singing their poems and odes, and with the passing of time, the scenes of the divine bird's sacrifice grew ever more vivid. Yet, my elder treats this as if it is a paltry thing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sounds like...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sorush got buttered up by honeyed words...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: What? No, impossible! I clearly wanted to imitate the divine bird because I was moved by its passion and will.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The only reason why I associated with the Order of Skeptics was because they would tell me about the happenings of years past... O—Of course, it wasn't like they didn't heap an appropriate amount of praise on me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's the same story, but told in an exaggerated way to get people's attention. Even Paimon likes listening to exciting stories!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! But if their intention was to record actual history, then they definitely did something wrong.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Indeed. Regardless if it is I or the humans of the Order of Skeptics, those who condition themselves to accept hyperbole as ordinary will see themselves become like this.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The Order of Skeptics's archives were no longer simple truthful records. Instead, they were filled with all manner of embellishments and subjective opinions.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...And, unknowingly, I began to put renown beyond action itself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like you finally get it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She seems more energetic than she was when she came here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isn't this a good thing? Hehe, now Zurvan won't be asking to take the Chaplet, will she?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your training is almost at its end. You'll definitely win Zurvan's approval!
